strings.name: Roger Penrose
strings.summary: Roger Penrose applied topology and geometry to general relativity, showing that gravitational collapse leads to spacetime singularities under appropriate conditions. He also developed twistor theory and nonperiodic tilings and wrote about physics, mathematics and consciousness. He received half of the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics. Some of his proposals concerning consciousness and cyclic cosmology remain disputed theoretical investigations.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2020. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced general relativity and black-hole theory, revealing important mathematical properties of gravitational collapse and spacetime structure.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: University College London mathematics bachelor's (1952); Cambridge mathematics PhD (1957)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Collapse and singularities
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Used global geometry and trapped surfaces to establish a singularity theorem and deepen understanding of black-hole formation.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Geometry and physics
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Developed twistor theory and nonperiodic tilings, contributing tools and questions to geometry and mathematical physics.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Received half the prize for showing black-hole formation to be a robust prediction of general relativity.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Published The Road to Reality
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Surveyed the mathematics and fundamental theories of modern physics in a substantial book.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Published The Emperor's New Mind
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Explored computation, physics and consciousness, presenting contested arguments about noncomputable processes.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Shared Wolf Prize with Hawking
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Recognized for research on spacetime structure and singularities.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Nonperiodic tilings
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Developed arrangements that tile the plane without translational periodicity, now known as Penrose tilings.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Oxford mathematics chair
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Became Rouse Ball Professor of Mathematics at Oxford and continued research on relativity and geometry.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Introduced twistor theory
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Proposed a geometric framework for reformulating spacetime and physical problems.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Gravitational-collapse theorem
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Proved a singularity result under conditions including trapped surfaces, extending beyond highly symmetric models.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Cambridge mathematics doctorate
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Completed algebraic-geometry doctoral research as his interests expanded toward theoretical physics.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: University College London degree
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Completed undergraduate mathematics before further study at Cambridge.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Colchester
